one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban writes a humble tribute to Maria Luisa 'Lou' Torres-Morales (June 21, 1944 - Sept 24, 2023), the wife of Dr. Dante Morales -- the brilliant cardiologist and director of Manila Doctors Hospital -- who passed unexpectedly. The news came via a phone call from his balae Linda Manalac ('Pare, our Kumare Lou died yesterday'); the author lost his balance and fell on a nearby chair, the way he had fallen on a chair in the Makati Med emergency room when his wife Leni died suddenly a few months earlier (he recalls embracing her covered body and sobbing 'I am sorry, honey, I failed you'). He reminisces about how Lou and Dan regularly broke bread with him and Leni during Sunday family lunches hosted by Tong and Linda. Lou was a quiet, attentive listener who turned small observations into thoughtful gestures: a gallon of buco-pandan sherbet after he mentioned liking it; dozens of corn cobs delivered after she watched Leni 'heartily munch her favorite corn cobs'; a Japan-trip Viber reminding them to bring winter wear; a perfectly-timed salabat suggestion when Leni had a sore throat; and weekly Viber messages -- many of them about the author's columns ('I can understand it even if I am not a lawyer. It was written in simple, clear, and easy English. I always look forward to reading your opinions') and many simply cheerful ('Have an enjoyable week ahead'; 'Please stay safe and healthy'; 'May your week be filled with fun and joy'). When Leni passed on April 9, Lou immediately wrote: 'Leni was such a wonderful lady. Yes, she was the epitome of a real fine lady in every sense of the word... How I wish I had given her a big tight hug the last time I saw her. We love you, Leni; you will always remain in our hearts.' The author admits that tears well in his eyes as he writes these reminiscences and that he could break into sobs if he continued, so he closes by summing Lou up: 'a true friend who was deeply compassionate, always thoughtful, always cheerful, humble to the point of self-deprecating, and loving to the point of self-sacrificing without expecting any requitement.' She did not burden others with her problems, always listened to friends' difficulties with a patient ear, and offered help across problems both small and big. He ends in prayer-address: 'Adieu dear Lou. Please say "Hi" to my Leni whom I am sure you will meet in heaven, and kindly extend my eternal love to her. And please prayerfully beg our Lord Jesus to bless and guide us here on earth whom you left behind, especially Dan. Until our joyful reunion in the Eternal Kingdom, we shall patiently bear our earthly pains and pines.'
